request_trace.user:
Generate a complete, production-ready k6 JavaScript test script.

## API Endpoints
GET /products - List products with pagination and filters (params: page, limit, category, status)
POST /products - Create a product (admin only) [body: application/json]
GET /products/{id} - Get product by ID (params: id)
PUT /products/{id} - Update a product (admin only) (params: id) [body: application/json]
DELETE /products/{id} - Delete a product (admin only) (params: id)
GET /cart/items - List current user's cart items
POST /cart/items - Add product to cart (merge and accumulate quantity if exists) [body: application/json]
PUT /cart/items/{itemId} - Update cart item quantity (params: itemId) [body: application/json]
DELETE /cart/items/{itemId} - Remove cart item (params: itemId)
GET /orders - List current user's orders (params: page, limit, status)
POST /orders - Create order from cart (requires non-empty cart, decrements stock) [body: application/json]
GET /orders/{id} - Get order by ID (owner only) (params: id)
POST /orders/{id}/cancel - Cancel an unpaid order (params: id)

## Configuration
- Virtual Users: 100
- Duration: 300 seconds
- Ramp-Up: 60 seconds
- Think Time: 500 ms
- Base URL: https://api.example.com
- Auth: none

## Requirements (all mandatory for a runnable, meaningful script)
1. `import http from 'k6/http'; import { check, sleep, group } from 'k6';` and `export const options` with `stages` implementing ramp-up then steady state (use Duration/Ramp-Up from Configuration; e.g. ramp 60s to 100 VUs, hold for the remainder).
2. NEVER hardcode the host. Build URLs from `const BASE_URL = __ENV.BASE_URL || 'https://api.example.com';`. Document: run with `k6 run -e BASE_URL=https://api.example.com/v1 script.js`.
3. If Auth != none: obtain a token in `setup()` (login call) and pass it to the default function; send it as `headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + token }` on protected endpoints. Document obtaining `AUTH_TOKEN` via `-e AUTH_TOKEN=...` when the token cannot be fetched inside the script.
4. Cover EVERY listed endpoint. For POST/PUT include a realistic request `body` taken from the endpoint schema (e.g. `{"name":"...","email":"...","age":30}`). Use `group('endpoint name', () => { ... })` per endpoint.
5. `check()` assertions: ALWAYS assert `res.status` against the expected code, AND assert at least one key response field (e.g. `res.json('email') !== null`). For error paths assert the error code field.
6. `thresholds`: set `http_req_duration: ['p(95)<500']` and `http_req_failed: ['rate<0.01']` (tune the 500ms to the agreed SLO if known).
7. Pacing: use `sleep(0 )` between requests to match Think Time; do not use long fixed sleeps as the only control.
8. `setup()` / `teardown()`: create any needed test data in `setup()` and DELETE it in `teardown()` so the environment is not polluted across runs.
9. No secrets hardcoded; never commit real tokens.

Output ONLY raw JavaScript. No markdown.
